docs.title: hw-check
docs.text:
Catch the mistakes that make an autograder score 0 — before you submit.

The CS1302A autograder compares your program's output against the expected string, character by character. Correct logic still scores 0 if the function name is misspelled, if a parameter is overwritten, or if the output format differs.

hw-check reads your file's syntax tree and reports those mistakes. It never runs your code, so it is safe even for a solution with an infinite loop.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install hw-check

Python 3.9 or newer. No third-party dependencies.

docs.title: First run
docs.text:
hw-check examples/broken.py --spec sum_even_digits

checking examples/broken.py  (spec: sum_even_digits)

  [ 1] Function name mismatch
       line 5: the spec asks for `sum_even_digits`, but the file defines
               ['um_even_digits', 'average', 'mean', '__init__']

  ...

  1 of 10 checks passed

  score: 1/10  — this may score 0

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 every check passed 1 at least one issue fired 2 the file is missing or cannot be parsed

docs.title: Use it from Python
docs.text:
from hw_check import check_file

for issue in check_file("solution.py", spec="sum_even_digits"):
    print(issue["id"], issue["rule"], issue["detail"])

docs.title: Demo
docs.text: The one-minute walkthrough used in the presentation. Run it from the repository root.

docs.title: 0:00 — The claim
docs.text:
The autograder only compares strings. This solution is logically correct and still scores zero.

hw-check examples/broken.py --spec sum_even_digits

Nine rules fire. score: 1/10 — this may score 0.

docs.title: 0:15 — Point at the first one
docs.text:
[ 1] Function name mismatch
     line 5: the spec asks for `sum_even_digits`,
             but the file defines ['um_even_digits', ...]

One missing letter. The autograder imports sum_even_digits, gets an ImportError, and never runs the code.

docs.title: 0:30 — Point at the second one
docs.text:
[ 4] input() inside a function
     line 7: `um_even_digits` calls input();
             the autograder runs without a keyboard

The argument was already passed in. Reading it again blocks forever.

docs.title: 0:40 — Fix them
docs.text:
hw-check examples/clean.py --spec sum_even_digits

all 10 checks passed

score: 10/10

Exit code is 0, so it can sit in a pre-submit script.

docs.title: 0:50 — The close
docs.text:
pip install hw-check
hw-check my_solution.py --spec sum_even_digits

Three seconds, before you submit — instead of finding out from a zero.

docs.title: Screen recording checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Terminal font large enough to read at 1080p
  • [ ] --no-colour off (keep the colours)
  • [ ] Run broken.py first, then clean.py
  • [ ] Show the exit code with echo $?
  • [ ] Keep the whole thing under 70 seconds

docs.title: Rules
docs.text: Ten checks. Each one corresponds to a mistake that has actually cost marks.

docs.title: 1. Function name mismatch
docs.text:
The autograder imports your file and calls the name written in the question. One wrong letter and the import fails.

# the question asks for sum_even_digits
def um_even_digits(n):     # ✗
    ...

def sum_even_digits(n):    # ✓
    ...

docs.title: 2. No function defined
docs.text:
The file is a script: it runs from top to bottom and defines nothing. The autograder has nothing to call.

total = 0
for n in range(1, 11):
    total += n
print(total)               # ✗ no function at all

docs.title: 3. Parameter overwritten
docs.text:
The value the autograder passes in is discarded before it is ever used.

def f(times):              # ✗
    times = int(input())

def f(times):              # ✓
    ...

docs.title: 4. input() inside a function
docs.text:
The autograder runs without a keyboard. input() blocks forever or raises EOFError.

def f(n):                  # ✗
    n = int(input())

def f(n):                  # ✓ the argument is already the data
    ...

docs.title: 5. Parameter never used
docs.text:
Usually means the wrong variable is being read — a silent wrong answer.

def average(nums, weights):    # ✗ weights is never read
    return sum(nums) / len(nums)

docs.title: 6. print() inside a function
docs.text:
Printing sends text to the screen. If the question wants a return value, the function returns None and the autograder sees nothing.

def f(n):                  # ✗
    print(n * 2)

def f(n):                  # ✓
    return n * 2

docs.title: 7. print() with several arguments
docs.text:
print(a, b) writes one line. If the expected output is one value per line, this is a format mismatch — and a format mismatch is a zero.

def f(a, b):               # ✗
    print(a, b)            # "1 2"

def f(a, b):               # ✓
    print(a)
    print(b)

docs.title: 8. round() instead of fixed formatting
docs.text:
round(20.0, 2) returns 20.0, not 20.00. Fixed decimals are a formatting problem, not a rounding problem.

def mean(nums):            # ✗
    return round(sum(nums) / len(nums), 2)

def mean(nums):            # ✓
    return f"{sum(nums) / len(nums):.2f}"

docs.title: 9. __init__ returns a value
docs.text:
Python raises TypeError: __init__() should return None.

class Counter:
    def __init__(self, name):
        return name        # ✗

docs.title: 10. Attribute never stored
docs.text:
name = name creates a local variable and throws it away. The object ends up without the attribute, and every later self.name raises AttributeError.

class Counter:
    def __init__(self, name):
        name = name        # ✗

class Counter:
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name   # ✓
